  • 4 boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed
  • 2 cups baby potatoes, halved
  • 1 cup baby carrots
  • 1 red bell pepper, sliced
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • Fresh parsley, chopped for garnish

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Start by prepping your chicken thighs—trim any excess fat and pat them dry with paper towels. Drying the chicken is crucial because it helps the skin crisp up nicely in the air fryer. If the chicken is too wet, it will steam instead of getting that golden crust we want. This step sets the foundation for juicy chicken with a crispy outside, so don’t skip it.
  2. In a large bowl, toss the halved baby potatoes, baby carrots, and sliced red bell pepper with olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, dried thyme, salt, and pepper. Make sure everything is evenly coated. The olive oil not only helps the spices stick but also promotes that golden, crisp texture during cooking. If you rush this step, the seasoning won’t be distributed well and some veggies might taste bland.
  3. Add the seasoned veggies to the air fryer basket, spreading them out in an even layer. Nestle the chicken thighs on top, skin side up. This arrangement allows the chicken skin to crisp up from the hot air circulating above the veggies, while the veggies roast evenly underneath. Crowding the basket will cause steaming, so make sure there’s some space around the pieces.
  4. Set your air fryer to 400°F (200°C) and cook for 25-30 minutes. Halfway through cooking, around 15 minutes in, carefully shake the basket or use tongs to turn the veggies for even browning. This step ensures all sides get crispy and prevents any veggies from sticking or burning. If you skip this, you might end up with unevenly cooked vegetables.
  5. Check the chicken’s internal temperature with a meat thermometer; it should read 165°F (74°C) to be safe. If the chicken isn’t quite done but the veggies look perfect, remove the veggies and let the chicken cook a few more minutes. This prevents overcooking the vegetables while ensuring juicy chicken.
  6. Once cooked, transfer the chicken and veggies to a serving platter. Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before slicing to allow juices to redistribute, keeping the meat tender and moist. Resting is often overlooked, but it really improves the texture and flavor.
  7. Sprinkle freshly chopped parsley over the dish for a fresh, vibrant finish. The herb adds a nice brightness that balances the smoky spices and roasted flavors. This final touch makes the dish look inviting and adds a subtle flavor lift.
  8. Serve immediately with your favorite side or a simple green salad. The combination of crispy skin, tender chicken, and perfectly roasted veggies makes for a satisfying meal with minimal effort and cleanup. This is why I love one-pot air fryer meals so much!
  9. Clean your air fryer basket after it cools down to keep it in good condition and prevent flavor buildup. A quick wipe with a damp cloth or gentle scrub with soapy water works well. Proper maintenance ensures your air fryer keeps producing great results every time.

🥘 Ingredients

  • 4 cups fresh corn kernels (about 6 ears)
  • 1 cup heavy cream
  • 1/2 cup whole milk
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter
  • 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour
  • 1 tablespoon sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
  • Pinch of freshly grated nutmeg (optional)

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Start by shucking your ears of corn and carefully cutting the kernels off the cob. Fresh corn makes all the difference here, so try to get the freshest you can find. Use a sharp knife and work over a bowl to catch any juice. This juice is packed with flavor and will add natural sweetness to your creamed corn, so don’t toss it!
  2. In a medium saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Once melted, sprinkle in the flour and stir constantly to make a roux. This should cook for about 2 minutes until it bubbles and smells slightly nutty but isn’t browned. This roux will thicken the cream sauce and give it a silky texture without lumps.
  3. Slowly whisk in the heavy cream and milk, adding them gradually so the mixture stays smooth. Keep stirring as the sauce heats up to prevent lumps from forming. Bring it just to a gentle simmer—don’t boil or the dairy might curdle. The sauce will thicken as it warms, forming a luscious base for the corn.
  4. Add the fresh corn kernels and their collected juice into the cream sauce. Stir gently to combine and season with sugar, salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg if using. The sugar enhances the natural sweetness of the corn without making it overly sweet, while the nutmeg adds a subtle depth of flavor.
  5. Reduce the heat to low and let the creamed corn cook gently for about 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally. This slow cooking softens the corn just enough to be tender but still retain a bit of bite. Keep an eye on it to avoid sticking or burning at the bottom.
  6. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. If you want it richer, you can stir in a little more butter or cream at this point. The final dish should be creamy but not runny, with a balance of sweet and savory flavors.
  7. Remove from heat and let the creamed corn rest for a few minutes before serving. This helps the sauce set slightly and the flavors to meld. It’s best served warm, alongside roasted meats, mashed potatoes, or even as part of a holiday spread.
  8. If you want a smoother texture, you can lightly mash some of the kernels with a spoon or use an immersion blender for a few seconds. This step is optional but gives the creamed corn that classic silky feel without losing the fresh corn bite.
  9. Serve immediately in a warm bowl garnished with a little fresh chopped parsley or chives if you like. It’s a simple touch that adds a pop of color and freshness to this rich side dish. Enjoy with your favorite main courses!

  1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C) and grease a 9-inch square baking pan or cast-iron skillet with butter. This step is crucial because a hot oven and a well-greased pan help create that signature crispy crust that contrasts beautifully with the soft interior. If you skip preheating or greasing properly, your cornbread might stick or bake unevenly, so don’t rush this part.
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt until evenly combined. This dry mix forms the base of your cornbread and evenly distributing the leavening agent ensures a uniform rise. If you don’t mix well here, you might end up with pockets of baking powder or uneven texture.
  3. In a separate bowl, whisk the buttermilk and eggs together until smooth. The buttermilk not only adds tang but reacts with the baking powder to give the bread its tender crumb. Mixing the eggs fully ensures your batter will be uniform and rise properly.
  4. Slowly pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients, stirring gently with a spatula just until combined. The key is to avoid overmixing here because too much stirring develops gluten and makes the cornbread tough. You want a few lumps to remain for a tender texture.
  5. Fold in the melted butter and fresh corn kernels carefully. The butter adds richness while the fresh corn gives bursts of sweetness and moisture. Be gentle folding to keep the batter airy. If you add the butter too hot or mix aggressively, you risk deflating the batter or uneven distribution.
  6. Pour the batter into your prepared pan and spread it evenly with a spatula. This ensures even baking and a consistent crumb. Don’t over-smooth or press down hard, which can compress the batter and make it dense.
  7. Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes until the top is golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean or with a few moist crumbs. The baking time is important to develop a crisp crust while keeping the inside moist. Opening the oven door too often causes uneven rising, so try to resist.
  8. Remove from oven and immediately brush the top with a little extra melted butter. This step adds shine, flavor, and helps keep the crust tender as it cools. Skipping it might leave the top dry or dull-looking.
  9. Let the cornbread cool in the pan for at least 10 minutes before slicing. Cooling allows the structure to set so slices hold together nicely without crumbling. Cutting too soon can make pieces fall apart.
